fact: Africa50 and Bayobab (MTN Group) partnered in May 2023 to co-develop Project East2West, a US$320-325 million terrestrial fibre network linking landlocked countries to coastal cables, with the Republic of Congo among the 12 countries named (Kenya, South Sudan, CAR, Congo, Tanzania, Rwanda, Uganda, DRC, Mozambique, Malawi, Zambia, Angola); Africa50's investment committee approved it on 21 July 2023.

Xalam Analytics' January 2026 brief describes the Central African Backbone project as ongoing to expand Congo's fibre backbone, connecting to secondary towns and neighbouring countries; the brief gives no date for the work beyond its own January 2026 publication, taken as the date.

Xalam Analytics' January 2026 brief states that submarine cables have been deployed across the Congo river to connect Brazzaville and Kinshasa (DRC); no date for the deployment is given, so the brief's January 2026 publication date is used.

On 6 February 2023 the Central African Republic inaugurated its national fibre backbone and its interconnection with the Republic of Congo (via Bomassa), part of the 935 km of installed and operational fibre under the AfDB and EU supported Central African Backbone project, with a Congolese telecoms ministry representative present; the release says this component completes the Cameroon and Congo components.
